name: WACO cabin biplane (C-series / YKS)
variants: QDC / UIC / UEC / UKC / YKC (Standard Cabin)
OC / UC / QC / GC series (Custom Cabin)
Cabin biplanes with 210 to 450 hp radials
summary: Luxury four-to-five-seat enclosed-cabin biplane built from 1931 (Standard Cabin) through 1939 (Custom Cabin sesquiplanes); mostly seen at antique fly-ins and airshows.

wings: Biplane wings; the later Custom Cabin models are sesquiplanes with a noticeably shorter lower wing
Upper wing carries the split flaps
engines: Round radial engine (Continental, Jacobs, Wright or Pratt & Whitney) under a cowl
fuselage: Fully enclosed cabin with large side windows
Welded-tube fuselage with a rounded, faired shape
Fixed gear with spatted or faired wheels on oleo legs
tail: Aerodynamically balanced rudder and elevators with wire bracing

tellTales: Biplane with a fully enclosed cabin and a small lower wing
Lower wing noticeably smaller than the upper on the later models
Cowled radial and fixed spatted main gear

confusedWith.howToTell: The Staggerwing has the lower wing forward of the upper wing and retractable gear; the Waco has the upper wing forward and fixed gear.
The F-series has open cockpits; the cabin Waco has a fully enclosed cabin.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
